title: Nikhilam Mastery — 4-Digit Numbers Near 10000
learningGoals: Compute products of 4-digit numbers near 10000 using Nikhilam deviations
Handle cases where both numbers are below, both above, or one above one below 10000
Extend Nikhilam thinking to any convenient base including 5000
coreIdeas: Nikhilam: cross-add (or subtract) deviations for the left part; multiply deviations for the right part
For base B: product = (A+d₂)×B + d₁×d₂ where d₁,d₂ are signed deviations from B
Near-10000 right part has 4 digits; pad with leading zeros if the product of deviations is smaller

workedExamples.title: 10002×9998 (mixed)
steps: Right part: (+2)×(-2) = -4 → right part is negative, so borrow: 99999996

starterPractice.q: What is the deviation (deficit) of 9998 from 10000?
In Nikhilam near 10000, how many digits does the right part have?
State the Nikhilam rule for the left part.
starterPractice.a: Add one number to the deviation of the other

onboarding.welcomeMessage: Near 10000 — tiny deviations do all the work. Nikhilam goes large!

duolingoLessonArc.mission: Multiply 4-digit numbers near 10000 using signed deviations — both below, both above, and mixed cases.

reviewLoop.action: Show deviation table and recompute left and right parts separately

sessionFlow.coachHook: Every Nikhilam problem starts with deviations. Positive above, negative below!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Show a number line near 10000. 9997 is -3 below. 10003 is +3 above. Write d = number - 10000.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: '9997 minus 10000 is -3. That is its deviation.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Find the deviation of 9996 and 10005 from 10000.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Always subtract: d = number - base. Sign tells you above (+) or below (-).

exercises.questionText: Find the signed deviation of each number from 10000: (a) 9997 (b) 10003 (c) 9990

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Mixed Case — One Up, One Down
sessionFlow.coachHook: Opposite deviations! The right part goes negative — and we need a borrow trick.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'Opposite signs in deviations give a negative right part — subtract 4 from 10000 ten-thousands.'
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: For equal and opposite deviations: result = base² - d². For 10000: that is 10^8 - d².

sessionFlow.coachHook: The same Nikhilam rule works for base 100, base 1000, and base 10000. Only the right-part digit count changes!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Base 100: right part = 2 digits. Base 1000: right part = 3 digits. Base 10000: right part = 4 digits. Show 98×97 near 100, 998×997 near 1000, 9998×9997 near 10000.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'Right part digit count equals the number of zeros in the base.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Use the correct base and compute 998×997.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: For base 10^n: right part has n digits.

exercises.hint: d₁=-2, d₂=-3. Left=998-3=995. Right=2×3=6→006 (3 digits for base 1000).

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Final Challenge — Near 5000 Using the Deviation×2 Trick
sessionFlow.coachHook: 5000 is not a power of 10. But 5000=10000÷2. Use base 10000 and multiply deviations by the ratio!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: To multiply near 5000: use base 5000. Right part has 4 digits. Example: 4997×4998. d₁=-3, d₂=-2. Left=4997-2=4995. Right=6→0006. Answer=49950006. Verify: 4997×4998 = 4997×5000-4997×2 = 24985000-9994 = 24975006. Re-examine: actual answer is 24975006. The method needs adjustment for non-power-of-10 bases. For base 5000: left part = left × 5000, right part = d₁×d₂. So: 4995×5000+6 = 24975000+6 = 24975006.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'For base 5000: left part × 5000, plus right part.'
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Base Master badge — non-standard base conquered!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: For base 5000: product = (left part)×5000 + (right part). Verify 4998×4999: d₁=-2,d₂=-1. Left=4997. 4997×5000=24985000. Right=2. Answer=24985002.

exercises.questionText: Compute 4998×4999 near base 5000. Formula: product = (left part)×5000 + (d₁×d₂).
